title: Your friend Dante parks a C$3,000 bike in your hallway: 'Don't ask.' Sgt. Bev is asking around about a bike.

outcomes.text: Bev wheels it out with a pierogi in her teeth. Dante unfollows you. The bike's owner sends C$200 and a photo of the reunion.

options.label: Hide it, take C$400
options.cost: A stolen bike behind your coat

outcomes.text: You hang a coat over it. Bev knocks, peers, moves on. Dante pays C$400.
Coat over the bike, C$400 from Dante. Bev knocks again. She noticed the coat.

later.text: Remember Dante's bike? Bev came back with a clipboard. The bike was behind your coat. Two hours, and C$300 in 'storage fees' of her own.
later.headline: Developing: a stolen C$3,000 bike was found in {name}'s hallway. Sgt. Bev: 'It was behind a coat. A coat, hon.'

options.label: Wheel it to the precinct as 'found'
options.get: The bike gone, Dante none the wiser

outcomes.text: 'Found it on 31st.' Bev looks at you for a long time. 'Sure, hon.' The owner gets it back by dinner.
'Found it.' Bev: 'Found it, did you? Sit.' One hour, and she was right to.

title: Priya's new boyfriend stored six boxed laptops in your closet. 'Fell off a truck.' He offers you one.

outcomes.text: Priya reads the boxes, reads him, and reads him the riot act. The laptops leave. So does he.

later.text: Remember the laptops in the closet? Priya made you dinner: 'Thanks for not letting me date a warehouse.'

options.label: Take one, sell it
options.riskWhy: Six laptops have six serial numbers

outcomes.text: One laptop, C$1,200 in Woodside. The boyfriend calls you 'family.' Please don't.
C$1,200. The laptop's serial is on a list.

later.text: Remember the closet laptops? The one you sold was on a list. Bev followed it to your closet, where five more were waiting.
later.headline: BREAKING: Five 'fell off a truck' laptops found in {name}'s closet. Sgt. Bev: 'It's always a closet. Why is it always a closet?'

options.label: Charge him C$300 storage
options.riskWhy: Storing it is still storing it

outcomes.text: C$300 for 'storage.' You don't open the closet for a week.

title: A city inspector asks about the basement Teddy rents out illegally. Teddy mouths: 'C$600 off your rent.'

outcomes.text: The city moves the three guys somewhere legal, with a window. Teddy fixes your sink last, for a year.

later.text: Remember the basement? The three guys found you to say thanks. Their new place has heat. They brought you a pie.

options.label: 'What basement?'
options.cost: Three guys in a basement with no window

outcomes.text: 'Storage, I think?' The inspector leaves. Teddy knocks C$600 off your rent.
C$600 off rent. The inspector writes down your name, just in case.

later.text: Remember 'what basement'? The inspector came back with a flashlight. You lied on a city form: C$1,000 fine. Teddy pays his own.

outcomes.text: You stall the inspector, chip in C$200, and Teddy puts in a window and a smoke alarm. Inspector signs off. Teddy hugs you, briefly.

title: Teddy offers C$1,000 if you tell the inspector his basement apartment is 'your storage.' It has a bed.

outcomes.text: Teddy sighs, 'Fine,' and spends the weekend making it legal. He's quiet with you for a month.

options.label: 'It's my storage'
options.cost: A lie on a city form
options.riskWhy: Storage doesn't usually have a bed

outcomes.text: 'My storage.' The inspector notes the bed. 'For naps,' you say. C$1,000.
'My storage.' C$1,000. The inspector notes the bed, the microwave and the three guys.

later.text: Remember the basement 'storage'? The city fined Teddy and you: C$1,500 for a false statement. Lola calls it 'the nap room scandal.'

title: Your neighbor lifts boxes off stoops and resells them. He wants your lobby as the drop: C$700 a week.

options.label: Say no
options.get: A lobby with nothing in it

outcomes.text: 'Nah.' He shrugs and asks the guy in 3C. The guy in 3C says yes. Of course he does.

options.label: Set a decoy box with Sgt. Bev
options.get: A thief caught, a block grateful

outcomes.text: You leave a box of Sal's expired coupons on a stoop. Bev catches him mid-lift. The block throws you a little party.

later.text: Remember the decoy box? Lola got the story from Bev.

outcomes.text: Boxes in, boxes out. C$700. You learn to not read the labels.
C$700. Thirty-one boxes stacked by size in your lobby. Very tidy. Very visible.

later.text: Remember the lobby drop? A tracking number led Sgt. Bev straight to your lobby. Thirty-one packages, two hours on the bench.
later.headline: BREAKING: Thirty-one stolen packages found in {name}'s lobby, stacked by size. Sgt. Bev: 'Organized. I'll give them that.'

title: A stoop on 30th Avenue: eight boxes, nobody home. Your neighbor's 'pickup crew' is one short: C$300.

outcomes.text: You keep walking. You move one box behind a planter so nobody else gets ideas. Small things.

options.label: Do the hour
options.riskWhy: Every door has a doorbell camera now

outcomes.text: One hour, eight boxes, C$300. You don't know what was in them. You don't want to.
C$300 for the hour. The stoop's doorbell camera got a lovely angle.

later.text: Remember the boxes on 30th? The doorbell clip is the block's group chat's favorite video. Bev booked you, the crew and the planter.

outcomes.text: The neighbor takes the boxes in. 'You're a doll.' Your pickup-crew neighbor calls you 'a cop's cousin.'
